newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 1.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 1.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$19.483 (+0.333)

BHP has told its annual results briefing that about 10 percent of its global asset base is underperforming, and that poor assets will put up for sale if they don't improve. Managing director John Prescott acknowledged that returns on capital and equity were inadequate.

Shareholders in the soft-drink bottler are expected to approve its A$3.4 billion share-swap deal with the San Miguel of the Philippines. Under the deal, San Miguel will take a 25 percent stake in the Australian-based bottler, while C-C Amatil will acquire San Miguel's soft-drink subsidary.

ICI Australia's British parent ICI Plc opens its offer of shares in ICI Australia to institutional investors. ICI Plc intends to sell its 62.4 percent interest in the Australian subsidiary. ICI Australia also launched the first stage on Monday of a planned appeal against a Federal Court decision that it had been negligent in relation to the pesticide Helix.

Macquarie Bank has been chosen as the successful bidder for the Federal government's automotive fleet management company DASfleet, with a bid of just under A$410 million, the Sydney Morning Herald reported. The paper said the purchase, which would make Macquarie one of the largest fleet leasing companies in Australia, would be announced by Finance Minister John Fahey on Tuesday.
